title: Red flags of business identity theft and impersonation | Middesk
summary: Discover the key operational red flags of business identity theft, unauthorized registry hijacking, domain spoofing, and executive impersonation in B2B onboarding.
body_markdown:
Corporate identity theft is a specialized commercial fraud scheme targeting established enterprises. Legitimate businesses spend years building trade credit, maintaining good standing with state registries, and establishing vendor relationships. Fraud operators target these enterprises to obtain credit or depository accounts without meeting any time-in-business requirement the lender applies.


Perpetrators extract corporate details from public Secretary of State registries, annual reports, and commercial directories, focusing on companies with active standing but infrequent administrative updates. Fraudsters misappropriate the entity's Employer Identification Number (EIN), formation filings, and trade references while diverting credit lines and loan disbursements to attacker-controlled accounts. The IRS lists unexpected tax transcripts or notices that don’t match anything the business submitted as warning signs of business identity theft.
